title: tk-studio asset manifest
description: Every asset a slice needs, declared once (Story 34.6, contract 0.1.29). The file lives at the project config's assets.manifest (default assets/manifest.yaml); each entry's file is derived, never declared: <assets.art_path>/<name>.glb (default art path art/greybox). `lib/assets.py check` validates it (names unique; tri_budget at least 12, a greybox cube) and gates every present file with `facts`; `lib/assets.py greybox` writes the greybox of every entry without one; `lib/assets.py match` and `generate` (Story 34.7) replace a placeholder on the cc0 and generated rungs once the facts gate and the visual gate pass.

categories.description: Optional overrides of the default category colours (prop #8a8a8a, character #d98c3f, environment #5b8c5a, vehicle #4a78b5, ui #c7b84a, fx #9a5bb5).

camera.description: The visual gate's camera (Story 34.7): yaw and pitch in degrees for the Workbench renders of the greybox and its replacement; default {yaw: 45, pitch: 30}.

name.description: The id and the file stem; unique in the manifest.

tri_budget.description: The triangle budget; `check` refuses one below 12 (a greybox cube).

bounds.description: The extent in metres on glTF axes (Y up: y is the height).

rung.description: The rung the entry is assigned to; status says which file is in place (a cc0 entry with status placeholder still stands on the greybox).

status.description: placeholder while the greybox is in place; candidate once a later rung's replacement has not passed both gates; accepted once it has.

source.description: Provenance for the cc0 and generated rungs (Story 34.7): `<kit>/<path relative to the kit root, forward slashes>` on cc0, `meshy:<task id>` on generated; empty on greybox. Written by `match`/`generate` when the replacement is accepted.

tags.description: Match tags for the cc0 rung (Story 34.7), a flow list [a, b]; default [].

prompt.description: The generator's prompt, read only on the generated rung (Story 34.7); default the name's words, then the category, then `low poly game asset`.
